clue.text: Partially opaque ductile waterway

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, so the answer sits inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Describes a canal that is cloudy and somehow malleable.
explanation.definitionFit: An aqueduct is a bridge or channel built to carry water, a man-made watercourse.

clue.text: Dying CO leaves instruction

indicators.note: the commanding officer departs, so those letters are taken out of the longer word

blocks.note: commanding officer, printed as the abbreviation
coaching is instruction or training

explanation.surface: A commanding officer at death's door issues a final order.
explanation.walkthrough: Take CO away from the front of COACHING and what remains is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dying for something is to long or yearn for it, just as aching for it does.

clue.text: Free from a French embrace

blocks.note: un is French for a
a lock is a tight hold, as in a wrestler's grip

explanation.surface: Someone escaping the clutches of a Gallic hug.
explanation.definitionFit: To free something can mean to release it by opening its fastening, as with a key.

clue.text: Rapid rise produces state of collapse

indicators.note: to produce is to make or fashion, so the letters are worked into something new

blocks.note: the two words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An economic boom that ends in a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bubble bursting; 'produces' is the anagram signal and 'Rapid rise' the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A building in disrepair is neglected and falling to pieces, a run-down condition.

clue.text: Scores of small groups of players?

definitions.text: Scores of small groups of players?

blocks.clueFragment: Scores of small groups of players?
blocks.note: surface reading: many little teams of sportsmen

blocks.clueFragment: Scores of small groups of players?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the written music played by trios, quartets and similar ensembles

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scores' looks like a number (twenties) or sports results, but it means sheets of music; the players are musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Chamber music is classical music written for a small ensemble, one player to a part, originally for performance in a room.

clue.text: Preserve exotic meal doctor's tucking into

indicators.note: something exotic is strange and foreign, so these letters appear in an unfamiliar order
one item is eating its way inside the other, so it sits within it

blocks.note: the letters of meal rearranged
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A physician enjoying a foreign dish, with a suggestion to keep it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor's' reads as 'doctor is'; MB goes after the first letter of the rearranged meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To embalm a body is to treat it chemically so that it is kept from decay.

clue.text: Ideal student overcome by rage

blocks.note: the rage is the current fashion, the mode
L for learner

explanation.surface: A perfect pupil who nevertheless loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the student being overcome by the rage means it sits underneath it. 'Rage' means a craze here, not anger.
explanation.definitionFit: A model pupil or model husband is an exemplary one, a perfect example to follow.

clue.text: What spectators may take if bad light stops play?

definitions.text: What spectators may take if bad light stops play?

blocks.clueFragment: What spectators may take if bad light stops play?
blocks.note: surface reading: cricket fans annoyed when the umpires halt a match for poor light

blocks.clueFragment: What spectators may take if bad light stops play?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the idiom for disapproving, read literally as poorly lit sight

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, play is suspended when the light is too poor; the phrase for disapproval also describes the gloomy scene literally.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a poor or unfavourable opinion of something is the idiom, while the gloom makes everything hard to see.

clue.text: Driver's vehicle test stopped by wild riots

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters run riot into a new order

blocks.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for vehicles
the letters of riots rearranged

explanation.surface: A car's inspection is halted when rioting breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopped by' here means closed off at the end by the rearranged letters. The MOT (Ministry of Transport test) is Britain's yearly roadworthiness check.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist is a person who drives a car, so a driver.

clue.text: He guides Home Secretary crossing wood on island

indicators.note: the secretary straddles the wood, so it goes around it

blocks.note: H for home, S for secretary
elm is a type of wood
the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A senior politician on a trip to an island timber yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home Secretary' looks like a single title but splits into two abbreviations; 'on' sets the island after.
explanation.definitionFit: A helmsman steers a ship, guiding its course from the wheel or tiller.

clue.text: Plug opening at sea

blocks.note: to plug a product is to advertise it; an ad is a plug
a rift is a crack or gap

explanation.surface: Something about unplugging a hole on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at sea figuratively means confused and lost, just as drifting aimlessly means having no direction.

clue.text: Rail transport for state retinue

blocks.note: to state something is to express it
a train is a body of attendants following someone important

explanation.surface: A royal entourage travelling by railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast locomotive service stopping at few stations is rail transport of the quickest kind.

clue.text: Suitable place husband's found in Ulster church

indicators.note: the husband is located inside the other letters

blocks.note: Northern Ireland, often called Ulster
the standard abbreviation
Church of England

explanation.surface: A married man has discovered a suitable place in a Northern Irish church.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a role or position that suits someone, as in finding one's niche.

clue.text: Bush able to act cunningly

blocks.note: box is a shrub used for hedging
clever means able or bright

explanation.surface: A US president is capable of performing artfully.
explanation.walkthrough: Bush looks like the president's name but it is the shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: To box clever is a British idiom for acting shrewdly or using one's wits to gain advantage.

clue.text: Skilled workers coping with cuts?

blocks.note: surface reading: staff managing under budget reductions
setter's reading: tradespeople whose job is trimming people's hair

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts' suggests austerity, but the cuts are haircuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairdressers are trained professionals who style and trim hair, so cutting is their everyday task.

clue.text: WC a school ordered, not a high-speed type

indicators.note: putting things in order means arranging them afresh

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A school is told to install a lavatory, by someone who is in no hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: A slowcoach is someone who moves or acts sluggishly, the opposite of a speedy person.

clue.text: Weapon for shooting Spooner's top bird?

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts are exchanged

blocks.note: top is boss, and a crow is a bird; swap their opening sounds

explanation.surface: A gun for bagging the finest game bird, as a muddled cleric might put it.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow is a mechanical bow that shoots bolts, a medieval missile weapon.

clue.text: Capable of meeting with it

blocks.note: being up to a task means being capable of it
a date is an arranged meeting

explanation.surface: Someone able to handle an appointment, alongside it.
explanation.definitionFit: With it is slang for fashionable and modern, current with the latest trends.

clue.text: Consequence of queen backing action of strikers

indicators.note: going backwards, so the queen's letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: Elizabeth Regina
percussion is the striking of instruments, the drummers' work

explanation.surface: Fallout from the monarch supporting industrial action by workers.
explanation.walkthrough: The strikers look like workers on strike, but they are things that hit, as in drums.
explanation.definitionFit: Repercussions are the after-effects or unintended results of some action.

clue.text: Managed to secure one, not the original

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside

blocks.note: to manage is to cope
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded in getting hold of one, but it wasn't authentic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reproduced from another source is a duplicate, not the first version.

clue.text: Dismiss extremely regressive juvenile court

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its ends, so each of the next three words gives its first and last letters

blocks.note: first and last letters
first and last letters
first and last letters

explanation.surface: Throw out a youth tribunal for being backward-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' applies to all three following words, not just the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To reject a proposal or applicant is to turn it down or send it away.

clue.text: Little inclination to select suitable candidates

blocks.note: short means small in height
a list is a lean, as of a ship

explanation.surface: An employer who has small appetite for picking the right applicants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclination' reads as a desire, but it is a physical tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: To shortlist is to pick out the best applicants for further consideration, such as interview.

clue.text: Plot's last feeble twist

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is the one kept

blocks.note: end of plot
feeble means weak

explanation.surface: A story's limp final turn of events.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweak is a small pull or adjustment, a sharp twisting pinch.

clue.text: Agree to cutting revolutionary engine component

indicators.note: something cutting through another sits in its middle

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary
to OK something is to approve it

explanation.surface: Consenting to slash a radical's car part.
explanation.definitionFit: The choke is a valve in a petrol engine's carburettor that limits air to aid cold starting.

clue.text: Flash Gordon's third jacket

indicators.note: only the letter at position three of the name is wanted

blocks.note: a blaze is a sudden flare
third letter of Gordon

explanation.surface: The garment worn by the comic-strip space hero Flash Gordon.
explanation.walkthrough: Flash Gordon reads as one name, but it splits into a word and a source of one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A blazer is a smart tailored coat, often in school or club colours.

clue.text: Amateur team includes a reserve

blocks.note: lay means non-professional
taken as written
a side is a team

explanation.surface: An unprofessional squad picks a substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserve' looks like a substitute player, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay something aside is to save it or keep it back for later use.

clue.text: Ruins King's broadcast

indicators.note: broadcasting is transmitting by voice, so it is the sound that counts

blocks.note: Rex is Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch's radio address goes out amid devastation.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin something is to destroy it, as a storm destroys a ship.

clue.text: Precisely where the telegraphist may be concentrating?

definitions.text: where the telegraphist may be concentrating?

blocks.note: first meaning: exactly on time

blocks.clueFragment: where the telegraphist may be concentrating?
blocks.note: second meaning, read literally: a Morse operator's attention fixed on the short signals of the code

explanation.walkthrough: A telegraphist sends Morse code, made of dots and dashes, so their focus is literally on its short marks.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at exactly the right time, punctual to the second.
